Indian Standard

CODE OF PRACTICE FOR PACKAGING OF PAPER AND BOARD (First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the recommended practices to be adopted inthe packaging of common varieties of paper and board. Packaging practices for special types of paper like tissue, varnish, etc, are not covered in this standard. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The Indian Standards adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 1398 : 1982 4185 : 1989 5134 : 1977 listed below are necessary Title Packing paper, waterproof, bitumen laminated (second revision) Adhesive paper tapes @rst revision) Bitumen revision) IN REAMS impregnated paper (first 3.3 Bundle Packing The packets shall be made into bundles weighing up to a maximum of 75 kg each and wrapped into hessian cloth and stitched with jute twine. In monsoon season, two layers of waterproof bitumen laminated paper (see IS 1398 : 1982) or bitumen impregnated paper (see IS 5134 : 1977) or polylaminated wrapper may preferably be used before gummy packing for bundles in order to avoid moisture penetration. For coated paper a polythene wrapper should be used to wrap the paper before gunny packing, irrespective of the seasons. 3.4 Bale Packing In case of bale packing, the ream packets shall be packed in bales. The net mass of each bale shall not exceed 200 kg. Wooden boards or battens of a size not less than that of the package shall be used both at the top and bottom sides of each bale for protection after wrappingthe bale with hessiancloth and stitching with jute twine and then tied with steel strapping all round. The bales shall be tied with 4 steel strappings, 1 in the direction of length and 3 in the direction of breadth. 4 PACKING IN REELS

3 PACKING

3.1 Paper and board in sheets shall be made into reams and the ream mass reckoned on the basis of 500 sheets and wrapper only. Each packet shall consist of 500 sheets or submultiples of 500 sheets depending on the mass and type of paper and board both in flat and fold packing. 3.1.1 In fold packing, folded reams shall contain 20 quires, each of 25 sheets folded together. 3.1.2 The number of sheets in a packet determined on the following basis: shall be

4.1 Paper shall be rolled on a core of 70 to 75 mm inside diameter, about 10 mm wall thickness and of length corresponding to the width of the paper. The core ends shall be protected by inserting well fitting wooden plugs or plugs of any hard material, extending to about 75 mm into the core. The reel diameter and reel width shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.2 The reel shall be wrapped with either two layers of A grade mill wrapper of 100 gsm or one layer of A grade mill wrapper of 150 gsm all around, both on the reel face and on the ends. The packed~reels shall then be wrapped in hessian on all sides and stitched with jute twine. As an alternative, the reels may be wrapped with 4 layers of B grade mill wrapper of 100 gsm or 2 layers of B grade mill wrapper of 150 gsm. During the monsoon season water proof bitumen laminated paper or bitumen impregnated paper maypreferably be used before the hessian packing instead of only ordinary mill wrapper. 4.3 The reel ends shall be protected with corrugated kraftcircular discs or similar reel end discs so as to protect the edges during transit. The size of the disc should be bigger than the outer diameter of the reel so that it can be folded at the edges. 1

a)

Paper below 27 kg per 500 sheets shall be packed into packets of 500 sheets each; Paper from 27 kg to 54 kg per 500 sheets shall be~packed into packets of 250 sheets each; and Paper above 54 kg per 500 sheets shall be packed into packets of 130 sheets each.

b) 4

3.1.3 Boa~rd shall be packed in packets of 150 or 75 sheets each depending on the basis mass. Boards can also be packed in 72,100 or 144 sheets. 3.2 The packet as determined above (see3.1) shall be wrapped with mill wrapper of at least 150 gsm when one sheet is used and of at least 80 gsm when two sheets are used. The packet shall be pasted with kraft paper gum tape (see IS 4185 : 1989), 5 cm wide at the joints. Jute strings/twines shall not be used for binding the packets. The packet shall then be made into bundles.

IS 6211:

1993 6.1 Ream Packing Each ream shall bear a label to indicate the quality of the paper, ream size, ream mass, substance of paper (gsm), lot number, month and year of manufacture and price as per the statutory requirements. 6.2 Reel Packing Labels shall be put on the wrapped reel to indicate quality of the paper, reel size, reel mass substance of the paper, lot number, reel number and serial number of reel, etc. The direction of rotation of the reel for unwinding and the reel joints shall also be clearly marked on the reel end': 6.3 For both bundles and reels, full description of the material including lot number and direction for unwinding shall be clearly written/marked on the hessian cover, as well.

4.4 The reels shall be tied with steel strappings all around, two each at right angles laying along the diameter at the disc ends. 5 PACKING OF PAPER FOR EXPORT

5.1 Forbothreampackingandreel-packingforexport of paper and boards, the procedure mentioned in 3 and 4 shall be followed. In addition, the reams and reels shall also be wrapped with polythene coverings or waterproof bitumen laminated or bitumen impregnated paper. In all cases of export, the reel ends shall be protected with reel end discs. 6 LABELS 6.0 In all cases the package shall be clearly labelled or stencilled with the indication of the source of manufacturer and trade-mark unless otherwise specified by the purchaser.
